title: Eq Interface
concept: The Eq and PartialEq interfaces define equality comparison — `==` and `!=` operators work on any type that implements Eq.
why: Without Eq, you can't compare values with ==. Implementing Eq is essential for using types in collections, tests, and business logic.
tips: Always implement both PartialEq AND Eq for total equality — Eq is a marker interface
Use #[derive(Eq)] whenever possible — it auto-implements both PartialEq and Eq
Eq is required for Map keys — equality determines uniqueness
The != operator is auto-generated from eq — you only need to implement eq
common_mistakes: Implementing PartialEq but forgetting Eq — Map and Set won't accept the type
Comparing floats with == in eq — NaN != NaN violates Eq's reflexivity
Accidentally comparing object identity (memory address) instead of value equality
